message.content:
**Answer:**  
The most iconic and widely recognized sculpture of the 19th century is **the Statue of Liberty** (Liberty Enlightening the World). Completed in 1886, it has become a global symbol of freedom and democracy and remains the most celebrated 19th‑century monument worldwide.

Other notable 19th‑century works that were also highly influential include:

| Artist | Sculpture | Year | Significance |
|--------|-----------|------|--------------|
| Auguste Rodin | *The Kiss* | 1889 | One of Rodin’s first major successes, it helped establish his reputation in the late 19th century. |
| Auguste Rodin | *The Gates of Hell* | 1880–1917 (unfinished) | A monumental bronze work that became a cornerstone of modern sculpture. |
| Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux | *The Dance* | 1875 | A dynamic marble group that exemplified the exuberance of French sculpture. |
| Antonio Canova | *Psyche Revived by Cupid’s Kiss* | 1787–1793 (late 18th, but still influential into the 19th) | A masterpiece of Neoclassical sculpture that continued to inspire 19th‑century artists. |

While many of these works were celebrated in their own right, the Statue of Liberty’s combination of artistic merit, engineering innovation, and symbolic power makes it the most famous sculpture of the 19th century.
